To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the throughput of TCP-Tahoe is insensitive to the fast-retransmission threshold and is insensitive to the packet-loss probability, that TCP-Reno is insensitive to the number of duplicate ACKs required for triggering a fast-retransmit and is insensitive to packet-loss probability, and that TCP-NewReno, which is a considerable improvement, has its throughput increase with decreasing fast-retransmit thresholds and decreasing packet-loss probabilities.

(i) TCP-Tahoe and TCP-NewReno are the most robust to packet losses in a local network, (ii) TCP-Reno and TCP-Tahoe perform similarly in a local network when packet-loss probability is large, and (iii) the TCP-NewReno version of TCP is the most robust to random packet losses.

the performance of TCP is sensitive to the granularity of the retransmission timer, the threshold for triggering fast retransmit, and the number of duplicate ACKs needed to trigger fast retransmit; TCP-Vegas is a considerable improvement, and reducing the threshold for fast retransmit from three to one is very effective.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance analysis of TCP in the presence of packet losses in the local network environment.
understanding the performance of various TCP versions in a local network environment.
understanding the performance of TCP in a wireless link environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in a local network, TCP-NewReno with fast retransmit threshold of one is the preferred version of TCP.
TCP-NewReno performs the best, and TCP-Reno is the second-best choice.
TCP-Vegas, with the fast-recovery modification, is the best version for a local network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, when random loss occurs, the throughput performance is not significantly affected by the various protocol features, and that TCP-Vegas is not an improvement over TCP-Traffic Control Protocol (TCP)-Reno.

, in a local network environment with random losses, the throughput of TCP-Tahoe and TCP-Reno is not very different, but TCP-NewReno can be a substantial improvement over both.
